correctness.rationale: For fixed nonzero N the change A=4Na is bijective; the equation ax²−tx+N=0 has only nonzero roots and solvability is equivalent to t²−A being in Q0. For distinct nonzero A,B,C the degree-four and degree-six products of discriminants are monic and squarefree over the algebraic closure (odd characteristic), giving genera 1 and 2 and two rational points above infinity. The character sums are −1 minus the corresponding trace; the single quadratic sum is −1, since (t−y)(t+y)=A has p−1 solutions. Expanding the product of the three factors 1−χ gives p+1−τAB−τAC−τBC+τABC. Outside the roots its value divided by 8 is the uncovered indicator; at most six roots contribute at most 1/2 each. The resulting bound (p−23−10√p)/8 is strictly positive at 149 and increases thereafter. The separate direct-image enumeration exhausts each odd prime below 149 and each unordered distinct nonzero parameter triple. It matches every count and the entire orbit at 73. Since 8 has order three and is a square modulo 73 (64²=8), the square action gives precisely 36/3=12 unordered triples.
residual_risks: Prime fields and N≠0 only; no extension-field or ring assertion. The computation verifies only the finite census and orbit, with all larger primes handled by the trace estimate.
